speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the emergency department. I see you are presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; this is a critical finding in a newborn. To determine the cause, were you able to pass meconium within the first 48 hours of life?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Midgut Volvulus.

I have received your history, but the presence of bilious vomiting in a newborn is a surgical emergency. I need to immediately visualize the anatomy to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray, Upper_GI_Series.
